transcript: Ava (Account Executive): Before we wrap, I want to make sure we have the renewal path right. Marcus (VP Operations): The renewal is still our plan, but security needs the updated data-retention packet before they will clear it. Ava: I will send the updated data-retention packet by Friday, October 9. Marcus: Great. I will introduce you to Dana in procurement on Monday so you can confirm the paperwork. Nina (Customer Success): I will schedule the administrator training before October 20. Marcus: If the SSO rollout stays stable, I want to revisit the analytics add-on for our support team next quarter. The pricing has to fit inside the existing operations budget. Ava: Understood. I will include an analytics option in the follow-up, but I will keep it separate from the renewal decision. Marcus: That works. The immediate blocker is still the security packet.

analysis.summary: Northstar plans to renew once security receives updated data-retention documentation. Procurement introduction and administrator training are the immediate next steps, with qualified interest in a separate analytics expansion next quarter.

followUp.subject: Northstar renewal next steps
followUp.body:
Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the clear conversation today. I will send the updated data-retention packet by Friday, October 9. You will introduce me to Dana in procurement on Monday, and Nina will schedule administrator training before October 20.

I will also include a separate analytics add-on option for next quarter, without tying it to the renewal decision.

Best,
Ava

crm.summary: Renewal remains the plan. Security clearance depends on the updated data-retention packet. Procurement introduction and admin training are scheduled next; analytics is a qualified expansion signal for next quarter, conditional on SSO stability and budget fit.
